inputs.root_cause: Event 309's own exact_next_action named 'independent-oracle' as the next invariant, noting both formats already pass 5/5 via the existing oracle tool but each emits a schema-validation WARNING worth investigating first. Investigated the warning: oracle/schema/oracle-package.schema.json's additionalProperties:false rejected 3 fields (dependency_hashes, executor_config, profiles_not_applicable) used by ALL 26 oracle packages in the repo, confirming the schema was simply stale relative to an already-established, universal convention -- not a real defect in any package.
inputs.obligation_targeted: product-goal.yaml's own 'independent-oracle' completion invariant for ipynb and safetensors -- NOT a certification claim for either format as a whole.
inputs.acceptance_evidence: Added the 3 missing property definitions (plus a new $defs/profile_id reused by the new profiles_not_applicable field) to oracle-package.schema.json, purely additive and non-behavior-changing (schema validation is advisory/non-blocking per execute_oracle.py's own docstring; oracle case execution never depended on it). Re-running validation against all 26 packages revealed the schema's staleness is much larger (family enum missing ~7 values, corpus_refs/authority.specification_refs item types wrong, a couple of legacy packages missing required properties entirely) -- spans the whole 26-format portfolio including the pre-existing 20-format legacy system, not just ipynb/safetensors or the FF6 mission. Deliberately stopped here rather than chasing the full reconciliation: the warning is cosmetic metadata validation, unrelated to the oracle's own real PASS/FAIL verdict, which is what the 'independent-oracle' invariant actually measures. Recorded that verdict directly: both formats ALL_PASS 5/5.

execution_steps: 1. Re-ran tools.oracle.execute_oracle for ipynb, safetensors, and (for comparison) nrrd/xliff/ubl -- confirmed the schema-validation WARNING is universal, present for every format that uses dependency_hashes/executor_config/profiles_not_applicable, not specific to ipynb/safetensors.

2. Located the schema at oracle/schema/oracle-package.schema.json and the validator call site (execute_oracle.py::_validate_oracle_package_schema, TC-ORC-006) -- confirmed via its own docstring this is 'Non-blocking: callers print WARNING but do not crash', i.e. advisory metadata validation, not a gate on the oracle's own actual verdict.

3. Confirmed via a grep across all 26 oracle/formats/*/oracle-package.yaml files that dependency_hashes, executor_config, and profiles_not_applicable are used identically (same shape) in ALL 26 packages, not a handful -- a safe, high-confidence addition, not a guess.

4. Added the 3 property definitions to the schema (dependency_hashes: object with executor_hash/registry_hash/recorded_at; executor_config: object with required module/callable; profiles_not_applicable: array of {profile, reason}), plus a new $defs/profile_id (the same 17-value enum profiles.items already used, reused rather than duplicated) referenced by profiles_not_applicable's own profile field.

5. Validated the schema is still well-formed JSON and re-ran the oracle for ipynb/safetensors/nrrd/xliff/ubl: confirmed the FIRST reported schema error is now gone for all of them, but running the full jsonschema Draft202012Validator against all 26 packages surfaced a much larger set of pre-existing mismatches (family enum missing ~7 already-established values like 'ai'/'scientific'/'localization'/'business'/'3d'/'text'/'document'; authority.specification_refs and corpus_refs items are objects everywhere but the schema still says string; invalid_cases.expected_failure_stage missing 'PARSE'; abw/fodg appear to be missing several required top-level properties entirely; csv/fods/zst have additional unexpected top-level properties).

6. Assessed this fuller staleness as a genuinely large, whole-portfolio undertaking (spans the pre-existing 20-legacy-format system too, not just FF6's 6 formats) and deliberately did NOT attempt it this tick -- flagged clearly for a dedicated future pass rather than half-fixing it.

7. Reframed the actual 'independent-oracle' gate correctly: the invariant is about the oracle's own real PASS/FAIL verdict (does this format's own output match ground truth), not about whether its metadata YAML validates cleanly against a schema. Both formats already show a genuine, real ALL_PASS 5/5 verdict (oracle-run-summary.json), unaffected by the metadata-schema warning.

8. Wrote reports/certification/ipynb/independent-oracle-gate.json and reports/certification/safetensors/independent-oracle-gate.json recording the real oracle verdict, the depth histogram (D1=3, D0=2 for both -- an honest report, not inflated: D2/schema-level depth does not apply to either format), and a clear note on the separate, non-blocking schema-metadata warning and its scoped partial fix.
9. Ran the full 6-format regression (3767 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed) to confirm the schema change caused no regression anywhere.
